electoral_system: Closed-list PR: 305 seats in local constituencies plus 90 seats on 12 regional lists; electoral quotient = registered voters in the constituency / seats; remaining seats by largest remainder; no legal threshold (unchanged from the 2021 reform)
notes: UPCOMING — election not yet held as of 2026-09-16; no results. Parties: 27 parties are contesting according to Le Matin, Belpresse, Lebrief, Le Matin d'Algérie and Morocco World News (campaign piece); one Morocco World News item counts '28 formations'. Electorate: 15,801,162 registered voters on the lists closed 31 July 2026 (Belpresse/Lebrief; 54% men, 46% women; 55% urban, 45% rural). Interior Minister Abdelouafi Laftit had earlier cited a provisional figure of 'approximately 16.5 million' (Morocco World News, August 2026) — discrepancy between provisional and final figures noted. This is below the 17,983,490 registered in 2021, presumably after a list revision. Candidacies: 1,850 lists and 7,288 candidates (provisional Interior figures reported by Morocco World News, September 2026). Campaign: 10–22 September 2026. Line-up going in: the outgoing majority is the RNI–PAM–Istiqlal coalition of head of government Aziz Akhannouch (270 of 395 seats in 2021); all three seek to hold or expand their weight, and tensions between the allies surfaced before the campaign (Al Jazeera, 3 Sep 2026). Opposition: USFP, PJD, PPS, MP, UC, plus the left-wing PSU and FGD, which are running joint lists (Morocco World News). One report states the RNI is seeking a second term 'despite Akhannouch's withdrawal from its leadership' — not verified here. MP campaigned on a 'Contrat haraki' (Article19). Polls: no published opinion polls located; Moroccan law restricts publication of election polls in the run-up to the vote, and analysts (Arab Weekly, KAS) describe the PJD as lacking coalition partners and the left as divided. Turnout is widely described as the key test (Rio Times, Eurasia Review). Results timing: first official results expected during the night of 23–24 September 2026 (Belpresse); the Interior Ministry announced the full seat distribution the day after the vote in 2021.
